title: National POW/MIA Flag Act
official_summary:
National POW/MIA Flag Act

The bill changes the days on which the POW/MIA flag is required to be displayed at specified locations to all days on which the U.S. flag is displayed. (Current law requires the POW/MIA flag to be displayed only on Armed Forces Day, Memorial Day, Flag Day, Independence Day, National POW/MIA Recognition Day, and Veterans Day.)

summary.headline: A 2019 law expands the days on which the POW/MIA flag must be displayed at specified locations, from six listed holidays to every day the U.S. flag is displayed.
summary.what_it_does: Before this law, federal rules required the POW/MIA flag to be displayed only on six set days, including Memorial Day and Veterans Day. The law changes that so the POW/MIA flag must be displayed on every day the U.S. flag is displayed at those specified locations. The summary does not list the locations, so the exact places covered are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and families of prisoners of war and missing service members
who_it_affects.how: The POW/MIA flag, which honors those still unaccounted for, must now be flown at covered locations on far more days of the year.

who_it_affects.group: Staff who manage flag displays at covered federal sites
who_it_affects.how: They must display the POW/MIA flag on every day the U.S. flag is displayed, rather than only on the six listed dates.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 7, 2019. The summary does not describe a separate later start date.
